title: Testa v. South Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint held administratively out of order because South Florida Presbytery had not yet acted on the matter; no merits decision. Adopted 19 concurring, 1 not qualified, 4 absent.
first_summary: The SJC ruled Frank Testa's complaint against South Florida Presbytery administratively out of order because the presbytery had not yet acted on the matter. The adopted vote was 19 concurring, 1 not qualified, and 4 absent.
summary: The SJC held Frank Testa's complaint against South Florida Presbytery administratively out of order because the presbytery had not yet acted on the underlying matter, so no merits decision was reached. The case thus turns on prematurity rather than the complaint's substance; the sparse record does not describe the underlying dispute. The adopted vote was 19 concurring, 1 not qualified, and 4 absent. RE Donohoe was not qualified because he could not certify that he had read the necessary portions of the Record (OMSJC 2.3.b).
